requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

findings.claim: When SurrogateType is omitted, the collector unconditionally calls CreateContractlessMembers(type) and never inspects the formatted type's attributes. A referenced type marked [MessagePackObject], with [Key(0)] on one member and [IgnoreMember] on another, therefore gets a contractless string-keyed map containing every public read-write member instead of an integer-keyed formatter that excludes the ignored member. This violates the explicit acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T be honoured; the documented contractless fallback should apply only when T has no [DataContract] or [MessagePackObject].

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedMessagePackFormatterRequirementTests.HonorsMessagePackAttributesOnMetadataType. It compiles ProjectA.MyObject in a referenced assembly with [MessagePackObject], [Key(0)] Id, and [IgnoreMember] Secret, then generates the ProjectB formatter. The test currently fails on head because the generated formatter has no WriteArrayHeader and includes Secret; it passes when the no-surrogate path honours those attributes.

findings.claim: When no surrogate is supplied, the collector unconditionally builds a contractless string-key model and never inspects MessagePack attributes on T. For example, a referenced T marked [MessagePackObject] whose Value property has [Key(0)] gets a name-keyed map formatter instead of the required integer-key array formatter; [IgnoreMember] and member formatter attributes are likewise ignored. This violates the acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T are honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterCollectorReceiptTests.MessagePackObjectKeysOnReferencedTypeAreHonored. It places [MessagePackObject] and [Key(0)] on a type in a referenced compilation and asserts that the user-declared generated formatter uses WriteArrayHeader rather than WriteMapHeader; it fails on head because the collector emits a contractless string-key formatter.

findings.claim: Callback casting is computed from only T's directly declared methods. If T inherits IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver from a base class that explicitly implements OnBeforeSerialize and OnAfterDeserialize, hasCallbackReceiver is true but needsCast is false. The generated formatter therefore calls value.OnBeforeSerialize()/OnAfterDeserialize() without an interface cast, although those methods are not directly callable on T, causing generated-code compilation errors.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterCollectorReceiptTests.BaseTypeExplicitCallbacks_Compile. The formatted class derives from a base with explicit callback implementations; compiling the generator-updated compilation should have no errors, but fails on head because the inherited explicit implementation is overlooked when needsCast is calculated.

hunches.claim: MessagePack attributes on T are ignored unless the user separately creates a surrogate. When no surrogate is supplied, the collector always builds contractless name-keyed members, without checking for [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[IgnoreMember]. This violates the acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T be honoured: an attributed external type would serialize as a contractless map rather than using its declared keys and membership.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an execution test for an external T marked [MessagePackObject], with [Key(0)] on one member and [IgnoreMember] on another, and a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] without SurrogateType. Serialize T and assert a one-element integer-keyed array containing only the keyed member; the current implementation instead produces a contractless string-keyed map.

hunches.claim: The requirement that MessagePack attributes on T are honoured has no test: every round-trip test uses an unattributed external type, and the only manually attributed types are the surrogate and the containing type. A generator that always applies contractless string-key mapping, even to a [MessagePackObject] type with integer or renamed keys, would pass all added tests.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generated-formatter round-trip and wire-shape test for a T marked [MessagePackObject] with a non-default integer or string [Key], asserting the attributed layout is used instead of contractless member-name keys.

hunches.claim: The no-deserializing-constructor guard is untested. None of the generator tests declares a formatted class without an accessible parameterless constructor or expects NoDeserializingConstructor, so deleting the guard would not be noticed.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L11] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: The new attribute deliberately creates an explicit opt-in exception to the usual rule that metadata-only types are not analyzed or given formatters by the consuming assembly; the existing default behavior remains unchanged.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L11] records that referenced-assembly types ordinarily receive no analysis or formatter and that this is deliberate. Here generation occurs only for a consumer-declared class explicitly annotated with [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter], as required by REQ-2129, rather than for all metadata-only types.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Add the marker attribute with an optional SurrogateType property so Project B can supply MessagePack-specific keys and settings on a surrogate type mapped to T by property name. Code: In addition to basic formatter generation, the generator must resolve and validate the surrogate, read its MessagePack annotations, and apply them to T's corresponding properties; the attribute gains a public Type-valued SurrogateType surface.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Add only the marker attribute and generate a bodyless partial formatter, using contractless public-member serialization by default and honoring DataContract or MessagePack metadata already present on T, without adding any new configuration mechanism. Code: The public API contains GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute without SurrogateType; key and union customization is limited to metadata already on T (including DataMember and related attributes), and user-defined attribute copies receive no special recognition.
